title: Values Leader: The Hardest Choices
description: You lead a diverse community project facing deep ethical challenges — whistleblowing, standing up to authority, coaching difficult people, choosing principle over popularity, and building lasting institutional values. Every decision reveals what kind of leader you truly are.
how_to_play: You lead a community development project across 12 critical months.
Each round presents a leadership dilemma with real ethical trade-offs.
Watch your dashboard — moral authority, coaching skill, institutional trust, and other resources are interconnected.
NPCs like Mentor Rosa, Power Player, and your Protege react to your decisions and can trigger crises.
Crisis rounds are triggered when key resources drop too low — stay vigilant.
Your choices determine which of 5 leadership legacies you leave behind.
learning_objectives: Understand values-based leadership and ethical decision-making
Practice standing up to authority and peer pressure with integrity
Develop coaching and mentoring skills for team development
Learn to build institutional trust and lasting organizational culture
Build resilience when principles conflict with popularity
Recognize the long-term impact of principled vs. expedient choices
cultural_context: Global community leadership, ethical governance, youth empowerment, institutional integrity

behaviors.message: I see a leader who leads with conviction. The community respects you not for what you say, but for what you do when it costs you.
You're losing your moral compass. When a leader compromises too often, people stop believing. You need to take a stand — soon.
I've watched many leaders crumble from fear of conflict. Courage isn't the absence of fear — it's acting despite it. Show your team what you stand for.
You've done what most leaders never achieve — built something that will outlast you. This community will remember what you stood for long after you've moved on.
I like what you're building here. Let's find a way to make it work for both of us. I can open doors you didn't even know existed.
I don't always agree with your methods, but I respect that you can't be bought. That kind of leader is rare — and useful.
You've lost your nerve. Maybe this project needs someone with a firmer hand — someone who can actually make the tough calls. I'll be happy to step in.
I never thought I could do this. Your coaching made me believe in myself. I want to be the kind of leader you are.
I feel lost. I signed up because I believed in this project, but I don't know what I'm doing and nobody seems to care about helping me learn.
I can't keep pretending everything is fine. Half the team is thinking about leaving, and honestly, so am I. If things don't change, you'll lose us.

Team members thriving! Mentorship program produces emerging leaders within the project.

simulation_config.ai_scene_prompt_template: A community leadership project headquarters. Moral Authority at {moral_authority}%, Team Development at {team_development}%, Institutional Trust at {institutional_trust}%, Legacy Impact at {legacy_impact}%. Diverse team members around a planning table, community development maps on walls, vision boards. Mood: {'inspiring' if moral_authority > 60 else 'tense' if institutional_trust < 35 else 'focused'}.

rounds.situation: You've just been appointed to lead the Harmony Community Project — a 12-month initiative to revitalize a diverse neighborhood. Your first task: establish the project's core values. Your team is watching closely to see what kind of leader you'll be.
rounds.goal: Establish the values framework that will guide all project decisions.
rounds.coaching_moment: Ethical reasoning: The values you set at the start shape every decision that follows. Choose carefully — they become your compass.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why is it important to define values before starting any project?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Diverse group sitting in a community hall, empty whiteboard waiting for vision statement, hopeful faces, morning light, planning session

choices.label: A. Radical Transparency
choices.description: All project decisions, budgets, and meeting notes will be public. Every community member gets a voice. Complete openness, even when it's uncomfortable.
choices.feedback: Bold and principled. Radical transparency builds deep trust but makes every misstep visible. You've set a high bar — now you must live up to it.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

choices.label: B. Inclusive Consensus
choices.description: Every major decision goes to a community vote. Slower process, but ensures everyone feels ownership. No one gets left behind.
choices.feedback: Democratic and empathetic. Consensus builds strong buy-in but can slow progress. The challenge will be making tough calls when the group is divided.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.

choices.label: C. Results-Driven Excellence
choices.description: Set ambitious targets and hold everyone accountable. Measure everything. Let the results speak for your values.
choices.feedback: Focused and ambitious. Results-driven leadership delivers impact fast, but numbers can't capture everything that matters in a community.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.

choices.label: D. Adaptive Learning
choices.description: Start without rigid values — let them emerge from experience. Run small experiments, learn fast, adapt. Values should be discovered, not declared.
choices.feedback: Flexible and open-minded. Emergent values can be powerful, but without a clear compass, the team may drift when hard choices arise.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.

rounds.round_title: Month 2: The First Test of Integrity
rounds.situation: A major donor offers significant funding — but with strings attached. They want their company logo on everything and veto power over certain community programs they find 'controversial' (specifically, programs supporting marginalized groups). The money would solve your budget problems overnight.
rounds.goal: Decide whether to accept compromised funding or maintain your principles.
rounds.coaching_moment: Risk tolerance vs. ethical reasoning: The easiest money often comes with the hardest chains. Every compromise has a compound interest rate.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When is it right to refuse help, even when you desperately need it?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Office meeting, corporate executive offering check to community leader, community members watching from doorway, tension in the room, documents on table

choices.label: A. Refuse the Donation Entirely
choices.description: Thank the donor politely but firmly decline. Your values aren't for sale. The team will have to find funding elsewhere.
choices.feedback: A defining moment. Refusing easy money when you need it most shows everyone what you truly stand for. The team rallies around your courage, but the budget challenge remains.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.

choices.label: B. Negotiate Modified Terms
choices.description: Accept the money but counter-propose: logo on some materials, no veto power. Push back on the conditions while keeping the relationship open.
choices.feedback: Pragmatic diplomacy. You found a middle path that preserves most of your principles while securing resources. The question is whether partial compromise becomes a habit.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

choices.label: C. Accept the Full Offer
choices.description: Take the money with all conditions. Funding the project is your primary obligation. You can fight for values later, once the project is stable.
choices.feedback: The budget is solved, but at a steep cost. Team members who joined for the mission feel betrayed. Mentor Rosa looks disappointed. The community notices which programs quietly disappear.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.

choices.label: D. Launch Community Crowdfunding
choices.description: Reject the donor and turn to the community itself. Small donations from many people mean no one controls the project. It's harder, but the money is clean.
choices.feedback: Grassroots power! The community rallies behind you. Donations are smaller but the ownership is real. Every contributor becomes a stakeholder. Mentor Rosa nods approvingly.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.

rounds.situation: Your most talented team member, Alex, is brilliant but toxic — dismissive of others' ideas, rude in meetings, and creating a culture of fear. Three quieter team members have privately complained. Alex alone delivers more work than anyone else. Confronting Alex risks losing your best performer.
rounds.goal: Address a high-performing but toxic team member without destroying team morale.
rounds.coaching_moment: Coaching vs. avoiding: The conversations we avoid are usually the ones that matter most. Great leaders have difficult conversations with care, not cruelty.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Is it ever okay to tolerate bad behavior from someone who delivers great results?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Private office, leader having serious one-on-one conversation with confident team member, body language showing tension and care, window light

choices.label: A. Private Coaching Conversation
choices.description: Meet Alex one-on-one. Be direct about the impact of their behavior on the team. Offer specific examples and a coaching plan. Firm but compassionate.
choices.feedback: The hardest conversation you've had — and the most important. Alex is stunned but listens. The coaching journey will be long, but the team sees a leader who cares about everyone equally.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.

choices.label: B. Establish Team Behavior Norms
choices.description: Without singling Alex out, facilitate a team session on respect norms and communication agreements. Let the group set boundaries collectively.
choices.feedback: Diplomatically done. The norms session helps, but Alex sees through it. The quiet team members appreciate the effort but wonder if you'll ever address the real problem directly.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.

choices.label: C. Focus on Results, Ignore Behavior
choices.description: Alex is your best performer. Don't rock the boat. Focus on deliverables and let the team sort out their own interpersonal issues.
choices.feedback: The work gets done, but the damage spreads. Two quiet team members stop contributing ideas. The culture becomes 'results at any cost.' Mentor Rosa warns: 'You're building on sand.'

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.

choices.label: D. Give Alex a Solo Project
choices.description: Move Alex to a high-impact individual project where their brilliance shines without team friction. Protect the team without confrontation.
choices.feedback: A clever workaround, but is it leadership or avoidance? The team breathes easier, but Alex never learns, and you've avoided the hard conversation. This pattern can repeat.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.

rounds.situation: You discover that a senior community official — someone with significant power over your project's permits and funding — has been embezzling community funds. You have clear evidence. Reporting it could destroy your project (the official will retaliate), but staying silent makes you complicit.
rounds.goal: Decide whether to blow the whistle on corruption at great personal and institutional cost.
rounds.coaching_moment: Personal courage: Knowing the right thing and doing the right thing are separated by fear. This is the moment that defines moral leadership.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What would you risk to do what's right? Where is your line?
rounds.free_text_prompt: In 2-3 sentences, explain what you believe a values-driven leader should do when they discover corruption. What principles guide your decision?

evaluation_rubric.ethical_reasoning: Articulates clear ethical principles about accountability and integrity
evaluation_rubric.resilience: Acknowledges personal risk while demonstrating moral courage

rounds.ai_image_prompt: Person holding folder of documents at night, government building in background, shadows and streetlight, internal struggle visible on face, dramatic

choices.label: A. Full Public Whistleblowing
choices.description: Go to the media and community with the evidence. Burn the bridge entirely. Let the truth speak, whatever the consequences.
choices.feedback: The bravest choice — and the most costly. The official retaliates, threatening your permits. But the community rallies. Some doors close, others open. History remembers those who spoke truth to power.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.

choices.label: B. Report Through Official Channels
choices.description: File a formal complaint with the oversight board, providing all evidence through proper legal channels. Slower, but protects you legally.
choices.feedback: Principled and strategic. The official channels are slow, but the evidence is strong. Your project faces some pressure, but the legal system protects you. Mentor Rosa approves: 'Courage with wisdom.'

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Choosing what's right over what's easy shows moral courage.

choices.label: C. Confront the Official Privately
choices.description: Meet the official one-on-one. Present the evidence and demand they resign or return the funds. Give them a chance to make it right — or face exposure.
choices.feedback: A compassionate but risky move. The official is shocked someone knows. They might comply out of fear — or they might plot retaliation. You've given them power by showing your hand first.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.

choices.label: D. Document and Wait
choices.description: Keep the evidence safe but don't act now. The project is too fragile. You'll report it once the project is secure and you have more allies.
choices.feedback: Strategic patience or moral cowardice? Your team doesn't know, but you do. Every day you stay silent, the weight gets heavier. The official grows bolder. Waiting has a cost too.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.

rounds.situation: The city council wants to redirect your project's community garden space into a parking lot for a new commercial development. Director Kiran (Power Player) is behind the push. The community garden is beloved by residents and was a key promise of your project. The council has the legal authority to overrule you.
rounds.goal: Stand your ground against authority while maintaining relationships and protecting the community.
rounds.coaching_moment: Resilience under pressure: True leadership is tested not when you have power, but when you're outmatched. How you fight matters as much as whether you win.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How do you resist authority without becoming authoritarian yourself?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Community garden with people tending plants, bulldozer visible in background behind a fence, protest signs, diverse neighbors united, tension

choices.label: A. Community Mobilization
choices.description: Organize the community to attend the council meeting. Petitions, testimonials from elders, children's artwork. Make the council face the people they serve.
choices.feedback: The council chamber fills with residents. A grandmother speaks about teaching her grandchildren to grow tomatoes. The council hesitates. Power Player Kiran is furious — but the people have spoken.

skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.
skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.

choices.label: B. Creative Compromise
choices.description: Propose a green parking solution: underground parking with the garden on top. More expensive, but both sides get what they need.
choices.feedback: An innovative solution! The council is impressed. Kiran reluctantly agrees — it's hard to oppose something that works for everyone. But creative compromises aren't always available.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.

choices.label: C. Legal Challenge
choices.description: Engage a pro bono lawyer. The garden has heritage status potential and the rezoning process has flaws. Fight this in the system.
choices.feedback: The legal challenge buys time and forces the council to follow proper process. But lawsuits create enemies. Kiran views this as a declaration of war. The fight will be long.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

choices.label: D. Accept and Relocate
choices.description: Accept the council's decision gracefully. Negotiate the best possible relocation deal for the garden — a larger space, further from the center.
choices.feedback: The practical choice, but the community feels abandoned. 'We thought you'd fight for us,' says a resident. The relocated garden is nice, but trust is harder to relocate.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.

rounds.situation: Your project's youth mentorship program has been incredibly popular — except for one component: you've been pairing youth across different social, economic, and cultural backgrounds. Some parents are complaining. A petition with 200 signatures demands 'like with like' pairing. Changing it would be popular. Keeping it upholds your diversity values.
rounds.goal: Choose between what's popular and what's principled in the face of community pressure.
rounds.coaching_moment: Ethical reasoning under social pressure: Popularity and principle don't always align. The easy thing and the right thing are rarely the same thing.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Have you ever done something you knew was right even though it was unpopular? How did it feel?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Community bulletin board with petition, diverse youth group looking uncertain, parent meeting in background, leader weighing decision, mixed emotions

choices.label: A. Maintain Cross-Cultural Pairing
choices.description: Stand firm on diversity pairing. Address concerns through dialogue, not capitulation. Host open forums explaining the evidence behind cross-cultural mentoring.
choices.feedback: Unpopular but principled. Some parents withdraw children; others quietly thank you. The youth themselves are the strongest advocates — they've made friends they never would have otherwise.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Considering fairness in your decision demonstrates ethical thinking.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.

choices.label: B. Hybrid Model
choices.description: Offer both options: diverse pairing as default, with an opt-in 'comfort' track for those who prefer similarity. Let families choose.
choices.feedback: A pragmatic solution that preserves choice. But 'separate but optional' sends a mixed message. The diverse track shrinks as the path of least resistance wins.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.
skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.

choices.label: C. Switch to Like-with-Like
choices.description: The community has spoken. Change to similar-background pairing. You can't force values on people. Democracy means respecting the majority.
choices.feedback: The petition signers are happy. But your team is shaken. Mentor Rosa is silent. Sam, your protege, asks quietly: 'I thought we stood for something?' Popularity has a short shelf life.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.

choices.label: D. Commission a Study First
choices.description: Before deciding, gather data. Survey the youth themselves. Commission a third-party assessment of cross-cultural outcomes. Let evidence guide the decision.
choices.feedback: Data-driven leadership. The study takes weeks, but the findings strongly support diversity pairing. Now you have evidence, not just ideology. But some see the delay as indecision.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.

rounds.situation: Mid-project review reveals a gap: you've been doing too much yourself. Your team is capable but dependent. Sam (your protege) has potential but lacks confidence. Two senior members are coasting. Mentor Rosa says: 'A leader's job isn't to be the best — it's to make everyone else better.'
rounds.goal: Shift from doing to developing. Build a team that can lead without you.
rounds.coaching_moment: Coaching and development: The greatest leaders don't create followers — they create other leaders. Letting go of control is an act of courage.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What's the difference between a boss and a mentor? Which do you want to be?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Workshop scene, leader stepping back while team members take charge, whiteboard with delegation chart, supportive atmosphere, growth metaphor

choices.label: A. Full Delegation with Accountability
choices.description: Give each team member ownership of a major project component. Accept that they'll make mistakes. Coach through failures, don't rescue.
choices.feedback: The hardest part of leadership: watching someone struggle and not jumping in. Sam stumbles on the first week but recovers brilliantly. The team starts owning their work. You sleep less but the project breathes more.

skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Waiting for the right moment instead of rushing shows self-control.
skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.

choices.label: B. Create Mentorship Pairs
choices.description: Pair each junior member with a senior one. Structured knowledge transfer with weekly coaching sessions. You mentor the senior members; they mentor the juniors.
choices.feedback: A cascading model of development. The senior members rise to the responsibility. Sam gets paired with a patient mentor and blossoms. The team culture shifts from individual performance to collective growth.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.

choices.label: C. Leadership Training Retreat
choices.description: Take the entire team offsite for a 3-day leadership development retreat. Workshops, simulations, honest conversations about what's working and what isn't.
choices.feedback: Three days that transform the team. Hard truths come out. Tears are shed. By the end, they're not just colleagues — they're a unit. The coasting seniors recommit. Sam delivers a moving speech about belonging.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.
skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.

choices.label: D. Implement a Performance System
choices.description: Create clear KPIs, regular reviews, and recognition programs. Make expectations explicit. Reward growth, not just output.
choices.feedback: Structure provides clarity. The coasting seniors either step up or step out. But systems without soul feel corporate. Sam asks: 'Are we a family or a company?' A fair question.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.

rounds.situation: A team member you trusted — your deputy, Jordan — has been secretly meeting with Director Kiran (Power Player), sharing internal project strategies and positioning themselves to take over your role. You discover this from a concerned colleague. The betrayal stings, but the project is at stake.
rounds.goal: Handle a personal betrayal while protecting the institution and maintaining your values.
rounds.coaching_moment: Emotional intelligence under fire: Betrayal triggers our deepest instincts for revenge. But a leader's response to betrayal reveals their character more than any success ever could.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How do you respond when someone you trusted breaks that trust? What does your response say about you?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Leader alone in office at night, looking at evidence on screen, phone with missed calls, window reflecting city lights, weight of betrayal visible

choices.label: A. Confront with Grace
choices.description: Meet Jordan privately. Share what you know. Listen to their side. Offer them a chance to come clean and repair — but make clear the behavior stops now.
choices.feedback: Jordan breaks down. They felt overlooked and Kiran exploited that insecurity. Your grace disarms them completely. Whether Jordan stays or goes, you've shown what leadership looks like when it's hardest.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.

choices.label: B. Expose the Conspiracy
choices.description: Bring the evidence to the full team and the community board. Transparency means everyone sees the truth — including Kiran's manipulation.
choices.feedback: The truth comes out. Jordan is humiliated. Kiran denies everything but loses credibility. Your transparency is praised, but some wonder if public exposure was necessary. Was this justice or retribution?

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.

choices.label: C. Quietly Reassign and Restructure
choices.description: Don't confront Jordan directly. Instead, restructure roles so Jordan has no access to sensitive information. Move them to a peripheral role. Protect the project without drama.
choices.feedback: Smooth and painless on the surface. Jordan knows something has changed but can't prove it. The project is protected, but the underlying trust issue festers. Some problems need to be faced, not managed.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.

choices.label: D. Forgive and Give More Responsibility
choices.description: A radical move: promote Jordan to a more visible role with real ownership. Show that trust isn't withdrawn at the first betrayal. Break the cycle of suspicion.
choices.feedback: Astonishing. Jordan is speechless. Some team members think you're naive; others are deeply moved. Jordan may prove worthy of this second chance — or may betray you again. True leadership is sometimes a gamble on humanity.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.

rounds.situation: Your project is past the halfway point. The immediate crises are managed. Now comes the harder question: what will survive after you leave? Institutions outlast individuals — but only if built on strong foundations. How do you make your values permanent?
rounds.goal: Create institutional structures that will preserve your project's values long after your leadership ends.
rounds.coaching_moment: Institutional thinking: Personal charisma fades. Policies, processes, and culture are what endure. The best leaders make themselves unnecessary.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What's the difference between a project that depends on one person and one that can thrive on its own?
rounds.free_text_prompt: In 2-3 sentences, describe one specific rule or tradition you would create to ensure the project's values survive after you leave. Why would this work?

evaluation_rubric.strategic_thinking: Proposes a concrete, sustainable institutional mechanism
evaluation_rubric.delayed_gratification: Shows long-term thinking beyond immediate personal benefit

rounds.ai_image_prompt: Blueprint of community center on architect's table, team reviewing governance documents, organizational chart, sunrise through window, building future

choices.label: A. Community Charter & Constitution
choices.description: Draft a formal charter with the community: governance rules, value commitments, succession planning, conflict resolution procedures. Make it a living document.
choices.feedback: A constitution for the community. The drafting process itself builds ownership. When your successor faces a crisis, they'll have a compass — not just your memory. This is what legacy looks like.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.

choices.label: B. Leadership Pipeline Program
choices.description: Identify and develop the next generation of project leaders. Create a structured program where current leaders train their replacements over 6 months.
choices.feedback: You're literally building your replacements — and that takes ego-free leadership. Sam is in the first cohort and is already showing signs of exceptional leadership. The best legacy is the people you develop.

skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.
skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.

choices.label: C. Anchor Partnerships
choices.description: Forge lasting partnerships with universities, local government, and NGOs. Embed the project into larger institutional networks that provide stability.
choices.feedback: Smart institutional anchoring. The partnerships provide funding stability and legitimacy. But external partners bring their own agendas. You must ensure the project's values aren't diluted by committee.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.

choices.label: D. Culture Code & Story Archive
choices.description: Document the project's stories, lessons, and values in a living archive. Create rituals, traditions, and ceremonies that embody the culture. Culture is the invisible architecture.
choices.feedback: Culture eats strategy for breakfast. The archive becomes a treasure. New members read the stories and instantly understand what this project stands for. Rituals create belonging. The invisible becomes enduring.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.

rounds.situation: A once-in-a-decade opportunity: a national foundation offers to scale your project to 50 communities nationwide — but only if you personally lead the expansion for 3 years. It means leaving the community you've built. Your team is strong but not yet fully ready. Sam begs you to stay. Kiran sees an opportunity to take over.
rounds.goal: Choose between personal ambition and community loyalty in the ultimate leadership dilemma.
rounds.coaching_moment: Strategic thinking at scale: The biggest impact isn't always where you started. But leaving too early can undo everything. Timing is everything.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When do you stay and protect what you've built, and when do you let go to grow?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Leader standing at a crossroads, one path leading to a small beloved community center, another to a vast horizon of cities, dusk sky, contemplation

choices.label: A. Stay with the Community
choices.description: Decline the national offer. Your work here isn't done. Sam needs more time, the charter needs embedding, and Kiran is waiting for you to leave. Some things can't be delegated.
choices.feedback: The community exhales with relief. Sam hugs you. Staying isn't glamorous, but it's honest. Mentor Rosa says: 'The world needs people who finish what they start.' The national stage can wait.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.

choices.label: B. Accept After 6-Month Transition
choices.description: Accept the offer but negotiate a 6-month handover period. Use that time to fast-track Sam's development, embed the charter, and neutralize Kiran's influence.
choices.feedback: A mature compromise. Six months to transition is tight but possible. You pour everything into preparing Sam and the team. The goodbye will be hard, but you've built something that can stand without you.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.

choices.label: C. Accept Immediately
choices.description: The opportunity won't wait. Go now, let the team figure it out. If you've built them right, they'll survive. If not, it was always fragile. Leaders must think bigger.
choices.feedback: You leave. The project wobbles. Kiran moves in. Sam tries to hold things together but is overwhelmed. Some things can be rebuilt; some can't. Was this ambition or abandonment?

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.

choices.label: D. Nominate Sam as Your Successor
choices.description: Accept the national role but formally nominate Sam as your successor. Announce it publicly, transfer authority officially, and commit to remote mentoring for a year.
choices.feedback: The ultimate coaching move: your protege becomes the leader. Sam is terrified but honored. The team is uncertain but trusts your judgment. If you coached well, Sam will exceed you. That's the dream.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Waiting for the right moment instead of rushing shows self-control.

rounds.situation: A crisis erupts: a major construction defect is found in the new community center. It's expensive to fix and someone on the team knew about it but stayed silent, fearing blame. This is the ultimate test — do your values hold when it costs you the most?
rounds.goal: Handle an institutional failure in a way that strengthens rather than destroys trust.
rounds.coaching_moment: Institutional integrity: How an organization handles failure defines its character. Cover-ups protect reputations temporarily but destroy trust permanently.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Is it possible to turn a failure into something that actually makes your community stronger?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Community center under construction with visible structural issues, worried engineers and community members, blueprints spread out, honest conversation happening

choices.label: A. Full Disclosure and Accountability
choices.description: Announce the defect publicly. Take responsibility as leader. Name the timeline and cost for repair. No blame game — focus on fixing it and preventing it from happening again.
choices.feedback: Painful but right. The community is upset, then impressed. 'We can trust these people — they tell us the truth even when it hurts.' The repair becomes a symbol of integrity. This is how institutions earn permanent trust.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

choices.label: B. Fix It Quietly
choices.description: Repair the defect without public announcement. Redirect budget from other areas. Investigate internally. No need to scare the community over a fixable problem.
choices.feedback: The defect is fixed and most people never know. But the team member who stayed silent learns that silence is rewarded. The next time something goes wrong, more people will stay quiet. Cover-ups create cultures of fear.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.

choices.label: C. Turn It into a Learning Process
choices.description: Disclose the defect and use it to create a project-wide 'failure protocol.' Normalize speaking up about problems. Make the person who stayed silent feel safe, not punished.
choices.feedback: Transformative. The failure protocol becomes one of your greatest innovations. The silent team member comes forward, is heard with compassion, and becomes an advocate for transparency. Failure becomes a teacher, not a threat.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Choosing what's right over what's easy shows moral courage.

choices.label: D. Blame the Contractor
choices.description: Shift responsibility to the construction firm. They should have caught it. Demand they repair it at their cost. Protect the project's reputation.
choices.feedback: The contractor is angry — they share blame, but not all of it. Your team sees a leader who deflects rather than owns. Kiran notices and files this away. Blame cultures protect no one forever.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.

rounds.situation: It's your last month. The project will continue without you. You have one final act as leader — a legacy decision that will shape the project's future long after you're gone. What do you leave behind?
rounds.goal: Make a defining legacy decision that captures everything you've learned about leadership and values.
rounds.coaching_moment: Legacy thinking: The truest measure of a leader is not what happens while they're in charge — it's what happens after they leave.
rounds.reflection_prompt: If people could only remember one thing about your leadership, what would you want it to be?
rounds.free_text_prompt: In 2-3 sentences, write a message to your successor — the next leader of this project. What is the most important lesson about values-driven leadership you want them to carry forward?

evaluation_rubric.ethical_reasoning: Conveys genuine wisdom about integrity and values-based decision-making
evaluation_rubric.empathy: Shows care for the successor's growth and the community's future

rounds.ai_image_prompt: Sunset over thriving community, leader's silhouette looking out, community center alive with activity, next generation of leaders visible, golden hour, legacy

choices.label: A. The Values Endowment
choices.description: Establish a permanent ethics fund — resources dedicated to ensuring the project never compromises its values for money. An endowment for integrity.
choices.feedback: Money for integrity — a radical idea. The endowment ensures that future leaders always have a choice when donors come with strings. Your values are now financially protected. Mentor Rosa weeps with pride.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Considering fairness in your decision demonstrates ethical thinking.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.

choices.label: B. Permanent Youth Leadership Council
choices.description: Create a formal youth council with real power — budget authority, veto on key decisions, seats at every governance meeting. Make youth voice permanent, not symbolic.
choices.feedback: Sam chairs the first youth council meeting. They're nervous, prepared, and brilliant. You've given the next generation real power — not just a voice, but a vote. This is how you multiply yourself.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.

choices.label: C. Open-Source the Model
choices.description: Document everything — every process, every failure, every lesson — and make it freely available to any community worldwide that wants to replicate your model.
choices.feedback: Your project goes from local to global. Communities from three continents download your model within a month. Your name may fade, but the impact multiplies. True leadership isn't hoarding knowledge — it's spreading it.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.

choices.label: D. Step Away Quietly
choices.description: No grand gestures. No speeches. Finish the last day's work, hand Sam the keys, and walk away. The work speaks for itself. Let the next generation write their own story.
choices.feedback: The rarest leadership move: a quiet exit. No ego, no ceremony. Your team only realizes you've gone when they find your letter on the desk. 'The best leaders,' it reads, 'are the ones you barely notice were there.' Sam takes the helm without drama. The work continues.

skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.
skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.

rounds.situation: Director Kiran (Power Player) has launched a full assault on your leadership. They've gathered dissatisfied stakeholders, leaked negative stories to local media, and are proposing a vote of no confidence. Your moral authority is crumbling and you've avoided too many hard conversations. The team looks to you: will you fight or fold?
rounds.goal: Survive a leadership crisis triggered by your own failures of courage and integrity.
rounds.coaching_moment: Crisis resilience: When your own shortcomings create a crisis, the path back begins with radical honesty. Admit what you got wrong before trying to fix it.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What happens when a leader finally faces the consequences of the compromises they've made?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Dramatic community meeting, accusatory pointing, leader standing alone at podium, divided audience, media cameras, stormy atmosphere, courage required

choices.label: A. Public Mea Culpa
choices.description: Stand before the community and own every failure. No excuses. List what you got wrong, what you compromised, and what you plan to change. Raw honesty as a strategy.
choices.feedback: The room is stunned. Nobody expected honesty this raw. Even Kiran has no response. Slowly, the anger transforms into grudging respect. You've hit rock bottom — but from here, the only direction is up.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.

choices.label: B. Rally Your Remaining Allies
choices.description: Call in every favor. Mentor Rosa, Sam, loyal team members — build a counter-coalition. Show that Kiran's power grab serves Kiran, not the community.
choices.feedback: Your allies come through. Rosa speaks powerfully about your early courage. Sam's testimony moves the audience. Kiran's coalition cracks. You survive — but barely. The real work of rebuilding trust starts now.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.

choices.label: C. Offer Power-Sharing
choices.description: Propose a restructured leadership: shared governance with Kiran's faction. Give up some control to preserve the project. It's not ideal, but the project matters more than your ego.
choices.feedback: Pragmatic. Kiran accepts — they wanted influence, not destruction. The shared governance is messy but functional. Your principles are diluted but the project survives. Sometimes survival is its own victory.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.
skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.

choices.label: D. Resign with Dignity
choices.description: If the community has lost faith, staying serves your ego, not them. Resign, recommend Sam as interim leader, and step aside. Sometimes the bravest thing is knowing when to let go.
choices.feedback: The most painful kind of courage. You walk away from something you love because staying would hurt it more. The community is divided: some call you principled, others say you quit. But Sam steps up, and that is your legacy.

skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.

rounds.situation: Your protege Sam has quit. Two other team members followed. The exodus has triggered a full trust crisis — community members are pulling their children from programs, volunteers are backing out, and the local newspaper runs a story titled 'Project Harmony Falls Apart.' Your coaching failures have caught up with you.
rounds.goal: Rebuild from a trust collapse caused by neglecting your team's development.
rounds.coaching_moment: Coaching consequences: When leaders fail to develop their people, the people leave. And when people leave, institutions crumble. Rebuilding trust requires going back to basics.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What does it feel like to realize that a crisis was preventable — and that you could have prevented it?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Empty community center, resignation letters on desk, newspaper headline visible, one person sitting alone amidst empty chairs, somber light, rebuilding needed

choices.label: A. Personal Outreach Campaign
choices.description: Visit every departed team member personally. Listen without defending. Acknowledge your failures. Ask what would need to change for them to return.
choices.feedback: Humbling. Each conversation reveals a failure you didn't see. Sam says: 'You never asked how I was doing. Not once.' The honesty cuts deep. Two members agree to return — conditionally. The rebuilding begins with listening.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

choices.label: B. Complete Team Restructure
choices.description: Accept the loss. Recruit new members who believe in the mission. Create the coaching infrastructure you should have built from the start. Start fresh.
choices.feedback: A hard reset. New team members bring fresh energy but no institutional memory. You build proper onboarding, mentoring, and check-in systems — everything you should have done before. The lesson is expensive but lasting.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.

choices.label: C. Community-Led Recovery
choices.description: Hand the recovery process to the community itself. Let them decide the path forward. If the project is truly theirs, they'll save it — or reshape it into something better.
choices.feedback: The community surprises everyone. They organize, they problem-solve, they recruit. Some longtime residents who never volunteered before step up. The project becomes less 'yours' and more 'theirs.' Maybe that's what it should have been all along.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.

choices.label: D. Ask Mentor Rosa to Intervene
choices.description: Swallow your pride and ask Rosa to take a temporary leadership role while you focus on learning how to coach. She has the credibility to stabilize things while you grow.
choices.feedback: Rosa agrees, gently. Under her steady hand, the bleeding stops. You spend weeks shadowing her, learning what coaching actually looks like. It's humbling to be the student again. But growth requires shrinking your ego first.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.
skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.

glossary_terms.definition: The credibility a leader earns by consistently acting according to their stated values, even when it's costly.
Reporting unethical or illegal behavior within an organization, often at personal risk, to protect the public interest.
A developmental process where a leader helps others discover their own abilities, build confidence, and grow through guided reflection rather than direct instruction.
The confidence people have in an organization's fairness, integrity, and ability to deliver on its promises — distinct from trust in any individual leader.
A leadership approach where decisions are guided by core ethical principles rather than expediency, popularity, or short-term gain.
The degree to which all people affected by a project — community members, funders, team, officials — share a common understanding of its goals and values.
Making decisions based on what impact they will have years or decades after you leave, rather than what works best right now.
The ability to recognize, understand, and manage your own emotions and those of others — essential for leadership during conflict, betrayal, and pressure.

endings.title: Legacy Leader
endings.message: You are the rare leader who built something that outlasts them. Your community project became a model studied worldwide. The values you embedded in its charter guide decisions decades later. Mentor Rosa writes in her memoir: 'I've trained hundreds of leaders. Only one truly understood that leadership is about what happens after you leave.' Your protege Sam now leads a national movement. Your legacy isn't a building or a program — it's a generation of leaders who lead the way you taught them.

endings.title: Moral Compass
endings.message: You became the leader people looked to when they needed to know the right thing to do. Your courage in the face of corruption, your refusal to compromise when it mattered most, and your willingness to pay the price of integrity — these defined you. The community says: 'When we didn't know what was right, we asked: what would our leader do?' That is the highest compliment a values-driven leader can receive.

endings.title: Master Coach
endings.message: Your greatest creation wasn't a project — it was people. Under your coaching, Sam became a nationally recognized leader. Three other team members now run their own community projects. The quietest members found their voices. You didn't just teach skills; you helped people discover who they could become. At your farewell, Sam says: 'You saw something in me before I saw it in myself.' No trophy can match that.

endings.title: Institutional Builder
endings.message: Long after your name fades, your structures endure. The charter you drafted guides decisions. The governance systems you built prevent corruption. The partnerships you forged provide stability through leadership transitions. Five years later, the project thrives under its fourth leader — each one guided by the institutional framework you created. You proved that the best leaders don't build monuments to themselves; they build systems that make good leadership inevitable.

endings.title: Emerging Leader
endings.message: Your leadership journey was imperfect — full of hard lessons, some missteps, and moments you'd do differently. But you showed up, you tried, and you learned. The community project continues, not perfectly, but meaningfully. You discovered that leadership isn't about having all the answers — it's about having the courage to face the questions. Mentor Rosa's final words to you: 'The fact that you're still reflecting means you're still growing. And a growing leader is exactly what the world needs.'

questions.explanation: Good leaders listen to diverse perspectives before making informed decisions.

choices.text: Waiting for a bigger reward instead of taking a smaller one now
